llmVisionReview.summary: Riverside Youth Soccer has genuinely good seed content in a handful of screens — the 'Season registration fee' sheet ($125.00 USD, Leo Rivera, U10 Falcons spring season), the 'Guardian approval desk' (Mia Rivera, parent of Leo Rivera), the 'U10 Falcons roster' (jersey 14, waiver due before Saturday), and 'Saturday practice schedule' (9:00 AM, Riverside Field 3) all read like real product copy. But three of the eight workflows do not demonstrate themselves: soccer-waiver-document and soccer-team-discussion both open the identical 'Youth privacy record' surface that belongs to soccer-minor-redaction, so six of the 27 screens are the wrong workflow, and soccer-reminder-notification's action sheet is titled 'Guardian practice reminder' but its body is the 'Choose attendance' RSVP form. Nearly every 'start' capture is a mid-scroll Home-feed frame clipped at the top ('form state.' cut in half, 'Protected export includes roster metadata,' cut in half) rather than the workflow's entry point, and two start frames (team-discussion, team-roster) are the same feed position showing the same 'Team discussion thre…' card. Layered on top is pervasive verbatim duplication inside every action sheet — the same Team/Schedule/Privacy triad printed twice per screen — plus spec-language copy ('Member form captures labeled details, privacy c…', 'The saved result keeps status, history, and change actions visible for this community task.') and truncated card titles.

A reviewer looking at the waiver evidence has no way to tell they are in a waiver flow; the word 'waiver' does not appear anywhere on those two screens. State legibility is weaker still: most 'start' frames are arbitrary mid-scroll positions of the shared Home feed, with the top card sliced ('…form state.' on registration-payment start, 'Protected export includes roster metadata,' on export start), so there is no title, no step indicator and no 'not started' signal. Where completion IS signalled it is signalled well — 'Registration paid', 'Guardian approved', 'Roster opened', 'Team update saved' are distinct filled banners — but soccer-reminder-notification start and complete are visually the same screen (same 'Guardian practice reminder' header, same 'Team update saved' banner beginning), so start-vs-complete is indistinguishable there.

On soccer-team-roster action, 'Featured player — Leo Rivera, jersey 14…', 'Protected fields' and 'Team context' all appear twice. On soccer-registration-payment action, 'Registration — U10 Falcons spring season registration for Leo Rivera.' and 'Receipt' appear twice. On the redaction sheet, Team / Schedule / Privacy appear twice. The pattern also shows up between hero and banner on the completion screens, where the same paragraph is printed as both subtitle and banner body.
findings.requiredFix: De-duplicate the sheet composition so each context row renders once per screen; the second card should carry only content the first does not, or be removed.

findings.title: Most 'start' captures are arbitrary scroll positions with clipped top cards
findings.description: Six of the eight start rows capture the shared Home feed mid-scroll rather than a workflow entry point, with the topmost card sliced through its text. soccer-registration-payment start opens on the fragment 'form state.'; soccer-export-metadata start opens on 'Protected export includes roster metadata, redaction preview, checksum verification, and transfer progress.' with its heading cut off; soccer-waiver-document start and soccer-minor-redaction start open on bare 'Edit details' buttons; soccer-guardian-join-approval start opens on bare 'Request changes' / 'Approve request' buttons. soccer-team-discussion start and soccer-team-roster start are the same feed position submitted twice, both dominated by the 'Team discussion thre…' card, with a third of the viewport left empty below 'Local package details'. soccer-practice-schedule start devotes its lower two-thirds to the unrelated 'Season registration fee' payment card.
findings.requiredFix: Capture each start state at the top of that workflow's own surface, with its title, its not-yet-started status and its primary action all in frame, and no unrelated workflow card occupying the majority of the viewport.

findings.title: 'Team update saved' is reused as the completion state for four unrelated workflows
findings.description: soccer-practice-schedule complete, soccer-reminder-notification complete, soccer-minor-redaction complete, soccer-waiver-document complete and soccer-team-discussion complete all end in the same banner: 'Team update saved — The soccer update shows RSVP choice, reminder body, checksum or saved result, inbox preview, and protected data handling.' The sentence lists five unrelated capabilities and names none of the specific outcome, and on several screens it is printed twice (once as the hero subtitle, once as the banner body). It is also clipped by the bottom navigation bar on every occurrence. By contrast the workflows that do have specific banners — 'Registration paid — Leo Rivera registration is paid…', 'Guardian approved — Mia Rivera is active for U10 Falcons…', 'Roster opened — The U10 Falcons roster shows players, guardians, waiver status…' — read correctly, which shows the specific pattern is achievable.
findings.requiredFix: Give each workflow a completion banner that names its own outcome and the resulting artifact (RSVP response and attendance count; reminder sent time and recipient count; fields redacted; waiver signed by and when; export file, size and checksum), and pad it clear of the bottom nav.

findings.title: Card descriptions read as acceptance criteria rather than product copy
findings.description: Alongside the good seeded copy, the scaffolding text is written as requirements-doc assertions: 'Payer, amount, privacy choice, entitlement, receipt destination, and retry/refund options are visible.' (registration action), 'Member names, roles, counts, status, and protected fields are visible according to persona.' (every roster sheet), 'The saved result keeps status, history, and change actions visible for this community task.' (four completion screens, naming no task), 'Title, date, time, location, host, capacity, and current attendance are visible before responding.' (practice action), plus the truncated generic 'Member form captures labeled details, privacy c…' used as the subtitle of two different feed cards and 'Another community role manages this item.' as the entire description of the waiver library. Sentences of the form 'X, Y, and Z are visible' describe the screen to a tester rather than speaking to a parent or coach.
findings.requiredFix: Rewrite all '… are visible' scaffolding lines as product copy that states the content itself, and replace the shared 'Member form captures labeled details, privacy c…' subtitle with per-feature descriptions.

findings.title: Action sheets describe controls they do not render
findings.description: Several action states name actions that are nowhere on screen. soccer-practice-schedule action and soccer-reminder-notification action both say 'Going, Maybe, Not going, and Change response remain available while the event is open.' with no such buttons rendered. soccer-guardian-join-approval action says 'Coach can approve, reject, or ask for a missing waiver before activation.' with no Approve or Reject button in frame. soccer-registration-payment action shows the payment summary but no pay button anywhere, even though the feed card behind it offers 'Pay and save receipt'. Separately, every feed card carries a 'Minimized' status chip — internal jargon that means nothing to a parent — alongside both a 'Tap for expanded view' control and a redundant 'Expand' button.
findings.requiredFix: Render the actual controls each sheet describes (RSVP buttons, Approve/Reject, Pay), and drop the 'Minimized' chip and the duplicate 'Tap for expanded view' / 'Expand' pairing in favour of one clear expand affordance.

findings.title: Team-roster surfaces use a slate-blue accent in a green-themed community
findings.description: soccer-team-roster action renders its app bar in slate-blue behind 'U10 Falcons roster', and soccer-team-roster complete renders the 'Roster opened' banner in the same slate-blue, while every other surface in Riverside Youth Soccer — app bar, section headers, completion banners on the guardian and schedule flows, bottom nav — uses forest green. The registration workflow separately uses purple. The result is three different accent families across one community's evidence set, with the blue reading as an unthemed default rather than an intentional category colour.
findings.requiredFix: Apply the community's green accent to the roster app bar and the 'Roster opened' banner, or document the colour-by-category scheme and apply it consistently across all eight workflows.

findings.title: Card titles ellipsise and content slides under the bottom nav
findings.description: Feed card titles are cut rather than wrapped: 'Guardian join and app…', 'Protected minor-data…', 'Waiver document libr…', 'Team discussion thre…', 'Youth soccer export …', and subtitles truncate mid-word ('Practice details include date, location, capacity, R…', 'You can read the current details without changing …'). Separately, content is clipped by the light bottom navigation bar on the majority of full-app captures — the 'Registration paid' banner, the 'Membership state' row, the 'Update roster' row, the 'Team update saved' body and the 'Team and roster view' card are each sliced horizontally. The 'Team' tab itself is cut off at the right screen edge on several frames.
findings.requiredFix: Allow card titles to wrap to two lines, add bottom padding equal to the nav bar height so no content is occluded, and fix the horizontal overflow that clips the 'Team' tab and the flush-left hero on the export complete screen.
